content.text: Every page in this record is the writer's own output, laid out by the outside reference. This paragraph is long enough that the reference has to break it across several lines, which is what makes a page boundary worth recording at all. The words after it are ordinary prose.

content.footnote: The footnote's own text, on the page the reference gives it.

metadata_excluded: the two dcterms dates in docProps/core.xml, which the writer stamps with the time it wrote the file
the document dates and the trailer's identifier, which the reference stamps with the time it ran
the document checksum the reference writes into the trailer, which covers those stamps
the whole XMP packet, which carries the reference's own dates and document identifiers and is replaced by a placeholder rather than read
the six-letter tag the reference puts in front of every font subset's name

the reference's own encoding of a face — the subset it splits the face into, the program, the widths and the character map of that subset — which the reference chooses differently from one run to the next; what a page drew in is recorded by the face's name and the face file's digest instead

engine_computed: the page numbers a table of contents prints

not_shown: commentary notes in the margin: the export states no comments, and a created document carries none
hidden text: the export draws only visible text
a link: it is drawn as its own text, with no target and no live link, so a page shows what the sentence says rather than where it goes
a table of contents' page numbers: the reference does not update the field, it shows the cached numbers the engine's own layout pass wrote
